The driver counts intercepted GETs per negative scenario and adds a ROUTE_NOT_HIT violation when the count is 0. The harness GREEN check requires exactly 4 scenarios with interceptedGets>0 and requires driver exit code 0. A spurious GREEN failure is unlikely: useOfficeQuery has no cache and refetches on every path change (src/modules/office/hooks/useOfficeQuery.ts:18-27), so every A->B switch issues the intercepted GET. In 'pending' mode the GET is held until after the button attempts, so the stale window really exists. A scenario that throws is never pushed, so the count drops below 4 and GREEN fails closed. The RED check is unaffected. Remaining minor gap: the positive controls still do not exercise 送審/退回. The office_e2e evidence is now pending_rerun, so no GREEN run with the new check exists yet.

new_findings.content: The derived Auditor verdict comes from AUDITOR_SNAPSHOT.json, a Builder-written transcription whose raw source reports are not in the repo. Nothing ties the transcribed verdict content to source_sha256; the hash string is just a field. Rewriting ASTRA-ROLL-001's verdict inside the existing CONTINUATION_V4 report entry to PASS/AUDIT_VERIFIED, with the hash left unchanged, and mirroring the change in the ledger plus a STATE resync, passes check_state --require-git with exit 0. ASTRA-ROLL-001 (HIGH) then drops out of open_critical_high. The validator cannot enforce 'Builder may never mark AUDIT_VERIFIED' while the Builder controls the snapshot. Mitigations: commit the raw Auditor files (or an Auditor-signed digest) and re-derive the snapshot in CI; or pin the per-ID verdict digest of each report in a file only the Auditor can change (CODEOWNERS or a protected path); or at minimum require any snapshot diff to come from an Auditor commit or signature.

A completely fabricated Auditor report is accepted. I appended a report with an invented source_sha256 ('1'*64) and a later generated_at, containing ASTRA-ROLL-002 PASS/AUDIT_VERIFIED, then pointed the ledger receipt at it. The checker accepts it because report_hashes is just the set of hashes in the snapshot, and the newest report wins. STATE.auditor_reports and latest_report_id are not compared against the snapshot either. Result: exit 0, PASS, and ASTRA-ROLL-002 (HIGH) is removed from open_critical_high. Mitigation: pin the allowed report IDs and hashes outside Builder control, or verify them against committed raw reports.

builder_status is not checked against the registry. RG-001 (HIGH; BLOCKED_DECISION in the v52 matrix) can be relabelled FIXED_PENDING_REAUDIT with closure_class BUILDER_FIXED_PENDING_REAUDIT and any verification_sha, and the check passes with exit 0. A pending human decision then shows up as 'fixed, awaiting reaudit' and closure_counts.HUMAN_DECISION_BLOCKED goes down. The finding stays in open_critical_high, so this is not a closure bypass, but it misrepresents gating state. The expected_class map only constrains closure for 4 builder statuses and never checks the status itself against registry status/status_map.

For non-PASS items, closure_class is not re-derived the way build_state.closure() does it. For example, ASTRA-ROLL-001 BUILDER_FIXED_PENDING_REAUDIT -> EVIDENCE_MISSING passes. Only AUDITOR_VERIFIED is gated, so the open lists stay correct, but closure_counts can be skewed freely. Running the same closure() logic in the checker would close this.

FIXTURES covers only web-ui/docs/enterprise/scenarios/*. Other files under docs/enterprise/ are still treated as documentation after pr_head and excluded from enterprise_verify/repo_coverage depends_on, even though CI or validators read them. These include docs/enterprise/architecture/roadmap.json (render_roadmap.py --check in enterprise-verify), docs/enterprise/uat/*.json (uat_evidence_index.py --check), docs/enterprise/v51|v52 registries, and AUDITOR_SNAPSHOT.json itself. They are inputs to checks, not product tests, so impact is low. CI on the new head would still catch a broken render or uat check, but the evidence SHA would not be flagged as stale.
